text.p: Base metal markets were hit by a wave of speculative selling during Tuesday afternoon LME trading, and with sentiment soft in copper, several were bruised at the close.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index rose 2.24 points to 239.92.

LME traders said the decline in copper was par for the course as the market is suffering from the summer slowdown, rising stocks and a move back into a cash/threes contango. Losses in aluminium and zinc were somewhat surprising, given current tightness. Key support held at $2,120, however, and by the close prices had clawed back some lost ground. Last trade was at $2,145, still down $17 a tonne from Monday.

Aluminium was slapped by fund selling as investment interests who bought metal when prices were rising from $1,600 a few weeks ago opted to take profits. The market managed to hold $1,630, but still ended at $1,634, down $43 from yesterday.

Zinc buckled during the afternoon when copper came under pressure, with liquidation driving the market down to a $1,461 low. A subsequent bounce helped cut losses, although final trade was at $1,477, still down $15.
Nickel was also rebuffed during the afternoon, and the current technical bounce is showing signs of running out of steam now. Last business was at an unchanged $6,670.
Lead hardly moved throughout the session, and appears immune to developments elsewhere. Prices are ranging above $600, with last trade today at $603, down $7.
Tin was also a passive onlooker to the main trend, with prices fluctuating quietly close to overnight levels. Last trade was at an unchanged $5,370.
Alloy moved lower with primary prices, and was indicated some $30 easier at $1,470/75.

IPE October Brent futures ended up 14 cents a barrel at $19.07 on Tuesday due to soaring United States gasoline futures and a blockage to Venezuela's main oil export route. "Gasoline was soaring. Brent got a tow higher but it slipped slightly at the end," said a floor broker. Dealers expect a bullish report from the American Petroleum Institute later on Tuesday showing falling stocks in the U.S. for the eighth consecutive week.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures ended a shade higher on Tuesday on spillover from strength in corn and on continued concerns about weather problems in other wheat growing countries, traders said. Wheat ended 3-1/4 to 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher with December up three at $3.75-3/4.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mixed Tuesday, in a low volume sequel to Monday's sell off, despite further gains in U.S. stocks and bonds after interest rates were left unchanged at the U.S. Federal Reserve's open market committee meeting (FOMC). In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $323.00/50, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $323.45 and the New York close Monday around $321.10/60 an ounce.
